original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: Review-and-compose of the two open T16 owner-map PRs on the selected PR1094 supplier (PR1407, PR2077), a bounded two-stage ejection-cycle search on PR1407's map (first version of this package), a longer cycle/LNS search with a min-diff re-assignment (second version), a global class-level repack (CP-SAT pattern/flow model per (capacity, window) class, max-flow realisation) followed by the cycle/LNS loop and a class-level min-diff re-assignment (third version), an evacuation LNS neighbourhood in the same loop (fourth version), and in this version class-level re-solves of a window + R4 model warm-started from the current map, each realised by a guided CP-SAT neighbourhood, followed by the class-level min-diff re-assignment toward the selected map at the same idle profile; plus a proved packing ceiling (at most 4,887 empty cap-48 bins and surrogate sum f ln f <= 908,139.013 for every legal map), stated in PROOF.md and checked by ceiling_bound.py. Widths, call order, windows and both suppliers are unchanged; only owner fields of whole helper roles change.
scope_change_reason: Self-selected, not drawn by scripts/choose_research_task.py: the session started as a review of PR1407 and PR2077 and whether their moves compose (they do not: every PR2077 subset is illegal on PR1407's map). The closest catalogue card is selected-packing. The search started from an unmerged PR's map (PR1407), but the shipped map is stated and verified only against the merged selected PR1094 map; PR1407 is lineage and credit, not a dependency.
bottleneck_link: Strictly decreases the complete complex moment of the binding complex supplier while preserving rank mass 1041408, deficit 5120, the local gauge44 supplier and the 144-call chronology.
stop_rule: kappa search: stop when the session's search budget ended (the class-level loop was still finding gains; no stall criterion was met). Min-diff: stop at a two-hour budget (the stage-1 MIP used 30 minutes; the LNS polish was gaining only a few relocations per round), followed by the strict replay, the independent seed67 audit, pricing, the majorization check and the ceiling check at the unchanged idle profile.
evidence: Unchanged PR1087 strict T16 replay passes all 11 stages with controls 69/12/6/15, actual_73column_sigmas 10011, kappa 0.001673614205725695 (conservative 0.001673614202872892): +5.7035e-4 relative over the selected record, +9.334e-7 over PR1407, +9.297e-7 over this package's first version (0.001672684510394236), +9.113e-7 over its second (0.001672702955495933), +5.600e-7 over its third (0.001673054161426948) and +2.723e-7 over its fourth (0.001673341928508063); 6.560% of the complex endpoint gap to the PR1240 ceiling a_hi = 0.001690054109089. The idle residual vector strictly majorizes the selected one (equal totals 237,024; checked mechanically by check.py), so the complex moment strictly decreases for any strictly concave per-residual weight. Seed67 auditor R1-R7, X1, X2 and its 11 controls pass; pinned-engine pricing and the PR1069 sweep agree. The map differs from the selected PR1094 map in 2,537 rows (2,170 relocated helpers, 367 offset-only). Proved packing ceiling (ceiling_bound.py, exact integers): every legal map has at most 4,887 empty cap-48 bins (this map 4,880) and surrogate at most 908,139.013 (this map 907,271.883); this bounds the surrogate, not kappa (the bound-attaining idle multiset prices at kappa 0.001674088611862992, indicative only). Conditional on the selected PR1094 inherited assumptions; no open-PR dependency.
author: Philippe Van Velzen
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance: PR review, composition test, search implementation (including the global repack and the class-level re-solve loop), min-diff re-assignment, the packing-ceiling proof checker, replay and packaging. No independent human review claimed.

open_questions.question: How much further does the finite search go on this supplier's T16 owner packing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The search was stopped while still improving; the class-level re-solve loop moved kappa by about 2.7e-7 over the fourth version. The proved ceiling leaves at most seven more empty cap-48 bins and 867 surrogate units.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun search/sloop.sh from data/OWNERS.json.gz toward a full winlp.py target under a memory cap, strict-replay each new best, then rerun the class-level min-diff.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute time; each new map needs the min-diff step and a strict replay again.

open_questions.question: What is the best attainable kappa from owner packing on the selected supplier's T16 windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The proved ceiling bounds the surrogate (908,139.013) and the number of empty cap-48 bins (4,887), not kappa. The bound-attaining idle multiset {1:2431, 17:1, 48:4887} prices at kappa 0.001674088611862992, but that is not a bound, and no concrete map is known to attain it.
open_questions.first_step: Check whether the bound-attaining idle multiset majorizes every attainable idle vector (which would make its price a kappa bound by Karamata), or state the knapsack relaxation directly in the exact per-residual cost.
open_questions.blocked_by: No kappa-level argument yet; the window + R4 class model attains the surrogate bound (solver-reported) but its solutions are not realised on concrete bins.

open_questions.question: Can the diff against the selected map be made smaller at the same idle profile?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Smaller diffs are cheaper to review. The class-level relaxation implies at least 1,548 relocations (solver-reported) and its own solution needs 1,583, against 2,170 shipped.
open_questions.first_step: Add distinct-call (Gale-Ryser) constraints to search/mindiff_cls1.py so that stage 1 stops proposing unrealisable class patterns (this version needed BAN for classes 9 and 25), and continue mindiff_lns2.py rounds from the shipped map.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute time; most of the gap comes from realising class solutions on concrete bins.
